title: Preemptive Soft-Reservation with Context-Aware Trimming
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a hybrid load-shedding mechanism that combines a very small preemptive token reservation pool for high-priority tenants with a context-aware trimming layer that can reduce per-request compute during overload without breaking contract semantics. The goal is to reduce SLA breaches during cross-region failover and noisy neighbor spikes while preserving highest-value requests and offering predictable degradation modes.
background: We frequently observe short, sharp load spikes during regional failovers and large tenant bursts. Current shedding strategies (pure probabilistic eviction or static priority queues) either over-reject or cause heavy quality regressions. Operators have expressed the need for: 1) a fast path to protect critical tenant requests, 2) graceful trimming so lower-priority work can still make forward progress, and 3) clear observability to tie degradations back to SLOs.
goals: 1) Implement a preemptive soft-reservation (small warm token pool) for critical lanes with predictable latency guarantees. 2) Implement context-aware trimming policies that can reduce token budgets, tokenized output length, or disable expensive features (e.g., reranking) per request. 3) Integrate with circuit breaker signals and multi-region failover routing so reservations migrate quickly to an active region. 4) Provide dashboards and SLO-linked alerts for observed degradation and customer impact.
out_of_scope: Full tenant billing changes, long-term autoscaling algorithm redesign, and model architecture changes (e.g., changing model size or quantization).
design: Key components: - Reservation pool: Per-region, small-sized token reservation for P0/P1 tenants (configurable, default 50 tokens per tenant). Soft-reservation means tokens are borrowed from a regional reservoir and reclaimed on overload using earliest-expire-first. - Admission controller: Uses reservation first, then falls back to a staged admission check (latency budget, estimated token cost, tenant weight). - Context-aware trimmer: Request-level plugins that can do one or more lightweight degradations in order: (a) drop non-essential tools/function-calls, (b) compress or truncate prefix/context, (c) disable reranking/ensembling, (d) request truncated/summary-only output. Each plugin exposes an estimated CPU/GPU cost delta. - Circuit relay: Circuit breaker emits a region-failover signal that triggers fast migration of reservation pointers and a temporary widening of trimming aggressiveness during the transition window. - Policy config: Declarative policy per-tenant and per-route describing priority, reservation eligibility, trimming budget, and fallback routes. - Observability: token-reservation utilization, number of trimmed responses, quality regression metrics tied to prompt-references, and SLO breach attribution for each tenant/route.
tradeoffs: - Soft reservations add complexity and state; may cause uneven fairness in global pooling. - Trimming reduces quality and requires careful per-tenant acceptable-degradation settings. - Fast reservation migration during regional failover risks double-spend if not bounded by coordination. - Small reservation pools protect critical traffic but do not eliminate systemic overload; must be combined with other autoscaling/fallbacks.
implementation_steps: 1) Add reservation pool data structure to admission service and expose admin API. 2) Implement admission decision flow that consults reservation then main token bucket. 3) Build plug-in interface for context trimmers and implement three initial trimmers (disable rerank, prefix prune, short-summary). 4) Wire circuit-breaker region-failover signals to reservation controller and trimming aggressiveness. 5) Add metrics/logging and a Grafana dashboard. 6) End-to-end tests and canary rollout to non-critical region. 7) Rollout to P0 tenants behind feature flag.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy to us-west-2, enable for internal tenant set, monitor token utilization and SLOs for 48h. Phase 2: widen to small set of customers with opt-in, tune trimmer thresholds. Phase 3: enable auto-migration for reservations on regional failover in controlled test. Phase 4: global rollout with per-tenant policies and UI controls in Console.
test_plan: Unit tests for admission logic and reservation accounting. Integration tests for trimming order and cost estimates. Chaos tests: simulate region failover with synthetic traffic and measure SLO breach delta. Regression tests: evaluate quality on held-out prompt set pre/post trimming. Load tests: spikes with mixed P0/P2 tenants to verify reservation protection.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics to emit: reservation_available, reservation_acquired, reservation_reclaimed, trimmed_response_count, trimmed_type_counts, admission_reject_rate_by_tenant, slo_latencies_by_tenant, failure_injection_traces. Alerts: reservation_exhaustion_high, trimmed_rate_exceeds_threshold, slo_breach_due_to_trimming. Dashboards: per-region reservation heatmap, per-tenant trim impact report, time-series SLO attribution.
acceptance_criteria: 1) During controlled 3x spike tests reservation-protected P0 requests maintain median latency within 1.2x baseline. 2) Trimmed responses increase but customer-facing SLO degradation limited to agreed thresholds for opt-in tenants. 3) No double-allocation of reservation tokens during simulated region failover. 4) Observability surfaces allow operator to identify top-3 causes of shedding within 10 minutes.
open_questions: 1) Should reservations be preallocated per-tenant or allocated from a regional shared pool with per-tenant caps? 2) How to express per-tenant acceptable-quality loss in a simple UI? 3) What is the canonical estimate for cost savings per trimmer action (needs benchmarking)? 4) What RBAC controls are required for tenants to opt into trimming?
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Spike analysis completed; determined 40-60 token reservation range is target based on 95th percentile traffic amplification.
2026-02-22: Prototype reservation accounting added to admission service; unit tests passing. PR opened: runtime/pull/2345.
2026-02-26: Implemented two trimmers (disable-rerank, prefix-truncate); initial integration tests show 18% average compute reduction for synthetic prompts.
2026-03-01: Began canary deployment to us-west-2 with internal tenants behind feature flag; monitoring dashboard instantiated.
